reasons: The management plan fields accept any content without checks.
Limits such as 1000 are not explained in the code.

terms.meaning: data transfer object, a shape that describes the data a route accepts
a fixed list of allowed values, such as a set of severity levels
a label written above a field that tells the framework how to check or document it

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the health input rules
sections.what: Brings in the enum lists from the database and the validation and documentation tools.
sections.why: Needed so every field can be checked against the shared database values.

sections.name: CreateVitalSignDto
sections.title: Vital sign input
sections.what: Describes a new vital sign reading: its type, main value, optional second value, unit, status, source, device, notes and measurement time. Values must be numbers between 0 and 1000.
sections.why: Likely reason: a shared rule keeps readings within a plausible range before they are saved.
sections.watch_out: The 1000 limit applies to every vital type, so a legitimate value outside it is refused.

sections.name: QueryVitalsDto
sections.title: Vital sign query filters
sections.what: Describes the filters for listing vital signs: type, start and end dates, page size from 1 to 100 and page number.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Paging keeps long histories from being sent in one response.
sections.watch_out: Page and limit values are converted from text, so a non-number will fail the check.

sections.name: CreateSymptomDto
sections.title: Symptom input
sections.what: Describes a new symptom entry: name, body area, severity, duration, frequency, triggers, related symptoms, notes and start time.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. The fields follow what a patient would normally describe.
sections.watch_out: Triggers and related symptoms are lists of text, so an empty list is accepted but a single text value is not.

sections.name: QuerySymptomsDto
sections.title: Symptom list filters
sections.what: Describes filters for listing symptoms: severity, date range, page size and page number.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Same paging approach as vital signs.
sections.watch_out: The severity filter only accepts values from the shared severity list.

sections.name: CreateConditionDto
sections.title: Chronic condition input
sections.what: Describes a new chronic condition: name, diagnosis codes, status, severity, diagnosis date, who diagnosed it, notes and a management plan.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Codes such as ICD-10 allow matching with medical records.
sections.watch_out: The management plan accepts any content, so it is not checked before saving.

sections.name: UpdateConditionDto
sections.title: Chronic condition update input
sections.what: Describes changes to a condition: status, severity, resolved date, notes and plan. Every field is optional.
sections.why: Lets a user change only the fields that changed.
sections.watch_out: Because every field is optional, an empty update is accepted without complaint.

sections.name: CreateDoctorNoteDto
sections.title: Doctor note input
sections.what: Describes a new clinical note: optional patient id, note type, title, the four clinical sections, codes, follow-up date and a confidential flag.
sections.why: Likely reason: the fields follow the standard visit note layout used by clinicians.
sections.watch_out: The patient id must be a valid UUID, and the confidential flag defaults to false but is not enforced elsewhere.

sections.name: QueryTrendsDto
sections.title: Trend query filters
sections.what: Describes filters for trend views: vital type, lab test name and a period of 7 days, 1 month, 3 months, 6 months or 1 year.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code. Matches the period choices used by the analytics service.
sections.watch_out: The period choices are written out here and also in the analytics code, so changing one means changing both.

summary: Defines the shape and validation rules for data sent to the health routes, such as vital signs, symptoms, conditions and doctor notes.
purpose: Rejects bad input before it reaches the database and documents each field for the API docs.
why: Reason not stated in the code. The validation layer is a common way to stop malformed or out-of-range data early.
how: Each class lists the fields a route accepts. Decorators mark required fields, check types, set numeric limits and enforce allowed values from enum lists. Swagger decorators describe the fields for the API docs.
inputs: JSON request bodies and query strings from the health routes.
outputs: Validated and typed objects handed to the controllers, or a validation error to the caller.
risks: Values are capped at 1000 for vital signs, so a bad reading above that is refused. Management plans are accepted as any shape. Several query fields are optional, so a bad date may pass if validation is switched off.
debug: If a request fails with a validation message, compare the field against the rules in this file. If a valid value is rejected, check the enum lists match the database enums.
